messages:

To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <m.singh@acme-procurement.com>, Acme Legal <contracts@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form draft + termination clause question

Rachel / Laura —

Thanks for sending the updated Order Form last week. Our legal team flagged the Term section: specifically the auto-renew language and the 60-day notice window for termination for convenience. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) Can Redwood accommodate a 90-day prior notice for non-renewal (instead of 60)? Our procurement cycle needs extra runway for approval.
2) We also need clarity on a mutual termination for convenience fee for the first 12 months — Acme typically requests either a pro-rated service credit or a termination fee equal to remaining committed fees.

I attached the annotated order form (OrderForm_ACME_v3_redlines.pdf) with inline comments. We're keen to keep momentum on the pilot but need commercial certainty on the exit mechanics.

Best,
Jordan
Director, Strategic Accounts — Acme Corp

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form draft + termination clause question

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the quick turnaround. A few points from our side after a prelim review: 

• Auto-renew: Our standard is an automatic 12-month renewal with a 60-day opt-out window. We can consider 90 days as a concession if Acme can commit to a 12-month minimum notice for any material change requests to the service during the renewal term.

• Termination for convenience (first 12 months): We cannot offer a full waiver of exposure in the first year. Options we can offer now: 
  - Pro-rated service credit for unused months (no additional fee), OR
  - Termination fee equal to 50% of remaining committed monthly fees (cap at 6 months) — this is our compromise path we use for pilot accounts.

• Implementation: to make this fast, we're attaching a short playbook and a redline tracker with two proposed inserts (see attachments). If Acme confirms which path (credit vs fee) you'd prefer, we can produce a clean order form for signature within 48 hours.

I've looped in Laura and Aditya for legal/finance alignment; Kimberly will validate SOW implications.

Thanks —
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachments: termination-playbook-notes.docx, redline_tracker.xlsx]

Subject: FW: Order Form draft + termination clause question (internal legal ops)

Team —

Quick internal note before we reply to Acme. Summarizing legal position and negotiation levers: 

1) Auto-renew / notice window
   - Business prefers to keep standard 60-day auto-renew opt-out to maintain capacity planning and pricing predictability.
   - Concession to 90 days is acceptable if Acme is willing to agree to a change freeze on major commercial terms during the notice period and to a 12-month minimum commitment on renewal (no mid-term pricing reductions).

2) Termination for convenience (first 12 months)
   - We should avoid a full pro-rated credit as a default; that shifts risk to Redwood.
   - Proposed middle ground: pro-rated credit + an implementation cost recovery fee (flat one-time amount equal to setup fees) OR the 50% remaining-fees fee with a 6-month cap as Rachel proposed.

3) Customer optics & escalation
   - If Acme pushes back, escalate to Sales Director for a one-time waiver (requires approval from Rev Ops). We can offer a 90-day notice and pro-rated credit if they commit to a 12-month paid renewal at signing.

Action items: Rachel to send consolidated options back to Acme with explicit callouts and a clean next-step (select A/B). Aditya to prepare a short approval note for Rev Ops if the customer requests a full waiver. Kimberly to price the setup/recovery amount if we include a flat fee option.

- Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form draft + termination clause question — proposal and next steps

Jordan / Maya —

Thanks again for the detailed feedback and the annotated PDF. To keep things simple and avoid multiple rounds, please pick one of the three options below for the Term / Termination mechanics and confirm which you prefer by EOD Friday: 

Option A (Customer-friendly):
- 90-day prior notice for non-renewal
- Pro-rated service credit for unused months on termination for convenience during first 12 months
- No additional termination fee

Option B (Balanced compromise):
- 90-day prior notice for non-renewal
- Pro-rated credit PLUS setup/implementation recovery fee (one-time flat fee: $15,000) on termination for convenience during first 12 months

Option C (Redwood standard compromise):
- 60-day prior notice for non-renewal
- Termination fee equal to 50% of remaining committed monthly fees, capped at 6 months

If you select A or B, we will need a signed commitment to a 12-month renewal term on the following renewal cycle (i.e., any renewal executed under this concession must be for a minimum 12 months). Option B pricing for the recovery fee is preliminary — Kimberly will confirm final amount when you indicate preference.

Next steps: once you confirm A/B/C, Laura will create a short addendum and we will send a clean order form for signature and DocuSign. 

Appreciate the quick decision here — want to keep pilot start date intact.

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
